subject.title: active-memory recall sub-agent gets 0 assembled messages, always times out

question: Is the deterministic circuit-breaker mitigation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100176 enough to proceed before live proof of the reporter's Codex/lossless-claw zero-output stack?
rationale: The issue is real and high impact, but current code shows the empty assembled-message count does not by itself prove an empty prompt, while the linked PR intentionally fixes only the repeated timeout tax.

options.title: Review mitigation first
options.body: Treat the linked PR as a bounded mitigation for per-turn dead time while keeping the root-cause proof requirement visible for zero-output recall.

options.title: Require live root-cause proof first
options.body: Pause the linked PR until a live active-memory plus lossless-claw run shows whether prompt projection, Codex app-server cleanup, provider behavior, or timeout classification owns the failure.

options.title: Fold into broader Active Memory reliability
options.body: Route this specific report under the broader active-memory reply-path reliability work if maintainers want one architectural fix rather than point mitigations.

recommendation.title: Review mitigation first
recommendation.body: Treat the linked PR as a bounded mitigation for per-turn dead time while keeping the root-cause proof requirement visible for zero-output recall.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the bundled Active Memory recall plugin and are the strongest history signal for deciding the plugin-side mitigation shape.
